File::StripNondeterminism is a Perl module for stripping bits of nondeterministic information, such as timestamps and file system order, from files such as gzipped files, ZIP archives, and Jar files. It can be used as a post-processing step to make a build reproducible, when the build process itself cannot be made deterministic. Title: Nondeterminism and Instability in Neural Network Optimization
# Nondeterminism and Instability in Neural Network Optimization. title = {Nondeterminism and Instability in Neural Network Optimization},. booktitle = {Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning},. series = {Proceedings of Machine Learning Research},. pdf = {http://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/summers21a/summers21a.pdf},. url = {https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/summers21a.html},. abstract = {Nondeterminism in neural network optimization produces uncertainty in performance, making small improvements difficult to discern from run-to-run variability. While uncertainty can be reduced by training multiple model copies, doing so is time-consuming, costly, and harms reproducibility. In this work, we establish an experimental protocol for understanding the effect of optimization nondeterminism on model diversity, allowing us to isolate the effects of a variety of sources of nondeterminism. Surprisingly, we find that all sources of nondeterminism have similar effects on measures of model diversity. To explain this intriguing fact, we identify the instability of model training, taken as an end-to-end procedure, as the key determinant. We show that even one-bit changes in initial parameters result in models converging to vastly different values. Last, we propose two approaches for reducing the effects of instability on run-to-run variability.}. %T Nondeterminism and Instability in Neural Network Optimization. %B Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning. %C Proceedings of Machine Learning Research. %U https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/summers21a.html. %X Nondeterminism in neural network optimization produces uncertainty in performance, making small improvements difficult to discern from run-to-run variability.
